findings.title: A view-only all-groups grant allows group creation
findings.body: `canManage()` accepts either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` on the all-groups resource. This method backs `requireManage()` for top-level group creation, so an administrator granted only permission to view all groups can create groups despite lacking any manage scope.

findings.title: Group view-permission lookup uses authorization resource IDs as group IDs
findings.body: `groupResource.getId()` is the authorization resource record ID, but `hasPermission` resolves its argument with `resourceStore.findByName`, and group resources are named with the group model ID. This therefore misses per-group resources and falls back to the all-groups resource; the subsequent addition of `groupResource.getId()` also supplies authorization IDs where user searches and counts expect group IDs. Administrators granted `VIEW_MEMBERS` or `MANAGE_MEMBERS` through group permissions can consequently get empty or incorrect user search results and counts.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients are not seeded with the Groups resource
findings.body: This lookup assumes the `Groups` type resource exists, but `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns immediately when a realm already has an admin-permissions client and only seeds schema resources and scopes when creating a new client. On upgrade, existing realms therefore lack the `Groups` resource and its new scopes; all-groups permission evaluation cannot find the resource (and may dereference null at the following lookup), leaving the new group authorization unusable for those realms.
